summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR142 crore (up ~80% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 9.96% on March raw-material spike.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR142 crore against INR79.1 crore a year earlier, driven by micro-irrigation and solar pumps demand. Q4 EBITDA rose 66% to INR14.16 crore, but margin slipped 86 bps YoY to 9.96%, which management attributed to a sharp raw-material price increase in March from geopolitical events. Full-year FY26 total income was INR419 crore (up 44%), with EBITDA of INR6.32 crore at an 11.03% margin, and the Ahmedabad plant is now operational. Management framed FY27 around solar EPC conversion, working-capital discipline and non-subsidy micro-irrigation mix.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR79.1 crore in Q4 FY25, ~80% YoY

segments.name: Micro-irrigation
segments.commentary: Core business; subsidy-driven bulk of revenue, cash/non-subsidy contribution around 15% in FY26. Export about 5% of micro-irrigation revenue, targeted to reach double digits in five years. Management guides 20-25% average growth over next three years.

segments.name: Solar pumps (EPC)
segments.commentary: Maharashtra order of about 1,500 pumps in first year there; a fresh 500-pump order worth about INR11 crore received this quarter. Q4 executed about 1,000 pumps and management targets at least 1,000 in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Solar rooftop (EPC)
segments.commentary: Expanded to multiple states under PM Surya Ghar Yojana; fully cash business per management. Targeted at tier-2 to tier-4 markets via the micro-irrigation dealer network.

guidance_outlook: Micro-irrigation growth target of 20-25% average annually over next three years.
Solar EPC contribution to rise from about 20% to about 50% of mix (equal to micro-irrigation) within next two years.
Ahmedabad plant full operation expected to lift micro-irrigation EBITDA margin by 1-1.5 percentage points in FY27.
Current micro-irrigation capacity (Rajkot, Kurnool, Ahmedabad) can deliver about INR400 crore revenue without additional capex for the next couple of years.
Working-capital intensity expected to stabilise in FY27 on receivable recoveries; capex intensity expected to stay modest.
capex_capacity: Ahmedabad facility (about 70,000 sq ft) is now operational; in-house manufacture of high-margin micro-irrigation components.
Existing capacity at Rajkot and Kurnool plus Ahmedabad can support INR400 crore micro-irrigation revenue without new capex for a couple of years.
Management said capex intensity remains low; incremental capital mainly working capital, which can be reallocated between segments.
Plans to seek PM-KUSUM empanelment in additional states during FY27.
demand_pricing: Solar pump order book is concentrated in Maharashtra and follows repeat state tenders; orders allocated on L1 basis with other bidders offered price-match, then quantum split by historical execution.
Solar pump execution window is typically 60 days; management says it has not missed timelines so far.
Management said solar pump margins are similar to micro-irrigation margins, so mix shift is not diluting profitability.
Network of about 750 dealers across major agricultural states supports fast execution for solar pumps and rooftop.
Micro-irrigation penetration is 17-18% of the 70 million hectare potential area, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin decline due to the shift toward solar EPC, which is structurally lower margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 margin drop was due to March raw-material cost increases, not mix; solar pump margins are roughly similar to micro-irrigation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR50 crore SBI credit line is drawn to backstop subsidy delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give the drawn amount; said total debt was about INR89 crore at end-March and 30-35% of bank limits remain unutilised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 split between subsidy and cash/retail sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation cash business was about 15% of FY26 revenue; rooftop solar is entirely cash business.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA uplift will the Ahmedabad plant bring?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation EBITDA margin expected to improve by 1-1.5 percentage points once the plant is fully operational this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the solar pump order book sustainable and what is its run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Unexecuted order is the recent 500-pump (INR11 crore) order; Q4 executed about 1,000 pumps and Q1 target is at least 1,000.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company supply irrigation accessories to third parties from Ahmedabad?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for now; focus is captive consumption, with third-party sales to be evaluated after captive scale-up.

risks_watch: Raw-material cost volatility (March 2026 spike) compressing EBITDA margin; Q4 margin at 9.96%.
Working-capital intensity and receivable recovery from state subsidy disbursements; reliance on bank limits (SBI INR50 crore line, drawn amount undisclosed).
Dependence of solar pump order book on Maharashtra tenders; new-state PM-KUSUM empanelment still pending.
Policy and subsidy timing risk on micro-irrigation and solar; competitive intensity in both segments.
Ahmedabad ramp-up and whether 1-1.5 pp margin uplift materialises in FY27.
Management did not disclose consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guidance or Q4 capacity utilisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and policy tailwinds, with explicit caution on subsidy timelines, competition and macro conditions. Evasive on quantitative items: declined to give drawn credit-line amount, utilisation percentage, and consolidated margin guidance.
key_quotes: The EBITDA margin came at 9.96% which was a slight decline of 86 basis points year-on-year and that was primarily on account of the sharp increase in raw material prices during the month of March due to unforeseen geopolitical events.

So, the solar pumps business, there is a very good order book and this gives us confidence that in the current year FY27 as well, we would be having a very good contribution and growth coming in from the solar EPC business.
So, definitely there is a good amount of under-penetration in this segment.
So, right now based on the current capacity, we can easily achieve INR400 crores without any additional capex for the next couple of years.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides micro-irrigation EBITDA margin up 1-1.5 pp in FY27 from the operational Ahmedabad plant, though Q4 consolidated margin fell 86 bps YoY to 9.96% on March raw-material costs and no consolidated FY27 margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Rajkot, Kurnool and Ahmedabad can deliver about INR400 crore micro-irrigation revenue without new capex for a couple of years, versus FY26 total income of INR419 crore, and Ahmedabad is already commissioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Micro-irrigation growth is guided at 20-25% average over three years, Q4 revenue rose about 80% YoY to INR142 crore, and Q1 FY27 solar pump execution is targeted at at least 1,000 pumps against about 1,000 in Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says capex intensity stays modest and existing capacity covers about INR400 crore of micro-irrigation revenue for a couple of years, though utilisation is undisclosed and PM-KUSUM expansion into new states is pending.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Record Q4 revenue of INR142 crore and a new 500-pump (about INR11 crore) order support upside, but no formal numerical guidance was raised and margin pressure is ongoing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw-material costs spiked in March, Q4 margin fell to 9.96%, and subsidy-disbursement delays and reliance on bank limits (INR89 crore total debt, 30-35% limits unutilised) are flagged risks.

rows.label: Solar EPC rising to about 50% of mix
rows.why: Management guides solar EPC share from about 20% to about 50%, equal to micro-irrigation, with solar pump margins said to be similar to micro-irrigation margins.

rows.label: PM-KUSUM empanelment in additional states
rows.why: Management plans to seek empanelment in more states, but the new-state approval is still pending and the solar pump order book rests on Maharashtra tenders.

rows.label: Working-capital intensity stabilises
rows.why: Management expects working-capital intensity to stabilise in FY27 on receivable recoveries, with total debt at INR89 crore and 30-35% of bank limits unutilised.

quality.why: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 80% YoY (INR142 crore vs INR79.1 crore), driven by micro-irrigation and solar pump demand, with the brief citing no one-off items; the brief does not split volume from price, so the driver is inferred as volume and the margin compression from March raw-material costs is a profit-side pressure rather than a growth one-off.
